item: The safe YAML loader choice is its own module, so the rings reader no longer drags the seed chain into the index engine
summary: PR #1432 made the keyword rings reader import the seeder's loader lazily; a full index pass then loaded nine modules of the seed chain that the engine identity neither hashes nor exempts, and tests/test_index_engine_stamp.py::test_every_module_a_pass_loads_is_hashed_or_triaged failed on main. Fix: the loader-class choice (libyaml's when the wheel has it, the pure-Python one when not; both safe) moved to src/utils/safe_yaml.py, which imports only yaml; seed_sources takes its _YAML_LOADER/_SAFE_YAML_LOADERS from it unchanged (its gc-paused catalogue parse and memo are untouched), equivalence.py imports it at module level, and the module is hashed in ENGINE_MODULES because the class decides how a ring file parses. No exemption was added. Hashing a new file changes the engine identity, as the earlier edit to equivalence.py already had. Measured ring parse 0.196 s against 1.272 s for yaml.safe_load, on a busy machine (a corpus generator was running); the quiet-machine figures stay 0.11 to 0.14 s against 0.98 s. Red without: tests/test_index_engine_stamp.py fails on main; new tests pin that the reader routes through the shared module, that seeder and reader use one class, and that the module imports nothing of the project. Not measured: libyaml absent (the fallback is the same two-class tuple the seeder already used).
